kidb1.intro: The Classical, Mar del Plata: White closes the centre, the knight reroutes, and Black starts the pawn storm with the f-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto. The dark-squared bishop belongs on the long diagonal.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal. This is the King's Indian.
e4 claims the centre. White has taken a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king sits behind the fianchetto.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
d5 gains space and attacks the knight on c6. White closes the centre and turns to the queenside.
Ne7 steps the knight off the pawn. From here it can support a kingside pawn storm.
Ne1 steps the king's knight aside so the f-pawn can move, and the knight can reroute.
Nd7 supports the pawn on e5 and prepares the kingside break.
f3 supports the pawn on e4 and gives the king a little air.
f5 attacks the pawn on e4 and starts the kingside pawn storm.

kidb2.intro: The Bayonet: White expands on the queenside, Black challenges with the a-pawn, and the rook takes back before the f-pawn goes.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
d5 gains space and attacks the knight on c6. That pawn move takes a share of the centre.
Ne7 steps the knight off the pawn and towards the kingside. It eyes the pawn on d5.
b4 starts the queenside expansion. This early pawn push is the Bayonet.
a5 attacks the pawn on b4 and challenges that expansion.
bxa5 takes the pawn on a5 and opens the queenside.
Rxa5 recaptures the pawn on a5. The rook comes to an active square.
a4 gains space and restrains Black's queenside.
b6 supports the rook and gains a foothold on the queenside.
Ba3 develops the dark-squared bishop on the a3-f8 diagonal, where it eyes the pawn on d6.
Nd7 supports the pawn on e5 and frees the f-pawn.
Re1 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the pawn on e4.
f5 attacks the pawn on e4 and starts the kingside pawn storm.

kidb3.intro: The Petrosian: White plays a pawn to d5 and a bishop to g5, Black kicks that bishop with the h-pawn and the g-pawn, and the knight comes to h5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the pawn on e5.
d5 gains space and closes the centre. This early closing is the Petrosian.
a5 gains queenside space and restrains White's expansion there.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6. The dark-squared bishop asks a question before Black can organise the pawn storm.
h6 asks the dark-squared bishop a question.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop on the pinning diagonal and steps off the pawn. It eyes the knight on f6.
g5 attacks the bishop on h4 and gains kingside space. The king's side is loosened, which this line accepts.
Bg3 drops the dark-squared bishop back and keeps it. It eyes the pawn on e5.
Nh5 attacks the bishop on g3 and offers a trade of Black's knight for that bishop.

kidb4.intro: The Classical with a trade on d4. Black leaves the e-file half open, the knight takes back, and the c-pawn challenges the centre.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and supports the centre.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and leaves the e-file half-open. Black chooses a fluid centre instead of a closed one.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight sits in the centre.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file, facing the pawn on e4.
f3 supports the pawn on e4.
c6 challenges the knight on d4 and prepares central play.

kidb5.intro: The Samisch: White plays the f-pawn, a bishop to e3 and the queen to d2, and Black expands on the queenside with the a-pawn and a rook to b8.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible.
f3 supports the pawn on e4 and keeps a piece off g4. This pawn move is the Samisch.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and opposes the bishop on g7.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Qd2 develops the queen beside the bishop on e3. White is ready to castle on either wing.
a6 prepares queenside expansion.
Nge2 develops the king's knight. The pawn on f3 has taken its usual square, so the knight uses e2.
Rb8 puts the rook on the b-file and prepares a pawn advance there.

kidb6.intro: The Four Pawns Attack: White grabs space with the f- and d-pawns, and Black blows the centre open with pawn breaks.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible.
f4 gains more space. Four pawns is a lot of centre to defend.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the broad centre.
d5 gains a wedge of space in the centre.
e6 attacks the pawn on d5 and chips at the wedge.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
exd5 takes the pawn on d5. The e-file is half-open.
cxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. White keeps a central pawn.
Re8 puts the rook on the half-open e-file. It eyes the pawn on e4.
e5 pushes the central pawn and attacks the knight on f6. The centre opens completely.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and accepts the open centre. It also eyes the pawn on f4.

kidb7.intro: The Fianchetto: both bishops sit on the long diagonal, Black plays the queen's knight to d7 and a pawn to c6, and the centre is traded on d4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
g3 prepares White's own fianchetto. White is not building the broad pawn centre at once.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal. It eyes the pawn on b7.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
e4 claims the centre in return.
c6 supports the centre and prepares the queen's path.
h3 takes g4 away from Black's pieces and gives the king air.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the pawn on e5.
Re1 puts White's rook on the same file, behind the pawn on e4.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the centre. It also eyes the knight on c3.
Nxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The knight replaces the pawn in the centre.

kidb8.intro: The Averbakh: the bishop comes to g5 and then f4, and Black challenges the centre with the c-pawn and the e-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bg5 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the knight on f6. This early bishop is the Averbakh.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre.
d5 gains a wedge of space. That pawn move takes a share of the centre.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question.
Bf4 drops the dark-squared bishop to an active diagonal and steps off the pawn. It eyes the pawn on d6.
e6 attacks the pawn on d5 and chips at the wedge.

kidb9.intro: The Exchange: the centre comes off, the queens are traded, and both sides bring out the remaining pieces.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
dxe5 takes the pawn on e5 and leaves the d-file half-open. White chooses an early exchange.
dxe5 recaptures the pawn on e5. The d-file is open.
Qxd8 trades queens and draws the rook to the open file. It also eyes the pawn on c7.
Rxd8 recaptures the queen on d8. The rook takes the open file, and White's king is still in the centre for the moment.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
c6 supports the centre and controls d5.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop. It eyes the pawn on a7.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight.

kidb10.intro: The Classical with the knight on d7. The bishop drops home, Black pushes the a-pawn and puts a rook on e8, and the dark-squared bishop takes back on d4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls the central squares.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
g6 prepares the fianchetto.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and supports the centre.
Bg7 puts the dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
e4 claims a broad pawn centre.
d6 keeps the centre flexible and prepares Black's central pawn.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Be2 develops the light-squared bishop and prepares castling.
e5 claims a share of the centre. It eyes the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports the pawn on e5.
Re1 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the bishop on e2.
c6 supports the centre and prepares a path for the queen.
Bf1 steps the light-squared bishop home and uncovers the rook on the e-file.
a5 gains queenside space and restrains a pawn advance there.
h3 takes g4 away from Black's pieces and gives the king air.
Re8 puts the rook on the e-file, behind the pawn on e5.
Be3 develops the dark-squared bishop and supports the centre.
exd4 takes the pawn on d4 and leaves the e-file half-open. It also eyes the bishop on e3.
Bxd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The dark-squared bishop takes the centre and opposes the bishop on g7.
